scenes.text: Imagine standing in a beautiful, fifty-mile strip of Yellowstone National Park where you could theoretically commit the perfect crime and easily walk away completely free.
This sounds exactly like a fictional thriller movie plot, but a bizarre constitutional loophole actually makes this real in a rugged, uninhabited area called the Zone of Death.

Because the United States Constitution strictly requires a jury to be selected from both the state and district where the crime occurred, and absolutely nobody lives there, a legal trial is literally impossible.

While the federal government desperately tries to avoid testing this loophole, the legal gap technically still exists today, so would you ever dare to camp in this lawless zone? Hit that follow button right now and tell me your thoughts in the comments below!
